# dsh-desktop-restart
English | 中文
> **Deprecated — merged into `@moonsand/dsh-ui-optimize`.** Reload and restart now live in dsh-ui-op
timize → *Settings → UI Optimize → Desktop actions*, alongside the theme gallery and sidebar panel f
olding. Install `@moonsand/dsh-ui-optimize` instead; this package receives no further updates. Runni
ng both at once is harmless (the route prefixes differ) but pointless — uninstall this one.
Two buttons in the sidebar foot of the **DeepSeek Harness desktop app**: reload the interface, or re
start the entire application (app + Host).
The production desktop shell ships no *Reload Page* menu item and no built-in accelerator for it, an
d it exposes no way to relaunch itself — `app.relaunch()` lives in the Electron main process and is
wired only to crash recovery. This plugin adds both, as ordinary sidebar actions.
[代码示例省略，未执行]
| Button | What it does |
| **Reload UI** | `location.reload()`. Reloads the page and every client plugin; the Host keeps runn

ing and turns in flight are not interrupted. |
| **Restart app** | Asks the Host to end every proces
s of the application binary and start it again from the same path. Second click to confirm; the labe
l turns red when Agent turns are running. |
## Requirements
- **Windows only.** The restart path is built on the Windows Task Scheduler and Windows Script Host.
- DeepSeek Harness desktop `0.2.1-rc.2` or newer (declared in `engines.dsh`; tested on `0.2.2-rc.1`

), Node `>=20`.
- No npm dependencies. `index.js` imports only Node built-ins; `client.js` imports `
react`, provided by the shell.

A package that is installed but **absent from `dsh.profile.bundles` silently does nothing**: it prod
uces no error and no button. Add the bundle entry, then restart the app.
The package ships its own `cordis.patch.yml`, which inserts the Host-side service, so no edit to the
profile patch layer is needed.
## Plugin market index (self-hosted)
`market/index.json` in this repository is a **format 1 plugin market index**, validated by DSH's own
`@deepseek-ai/dsh-plugin-market-index`. To see this plugin in the desktop app's **Plugins → Discove
eek-ai/dsh-plugin-market-index`. To see this plugin in the desktop app's **Plugins → Discover** tab:
1. Push the repository to GitHub; the index URL is `https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MoonSand/dsh-d

esktop-restart/main/market/index.json` (GitHub Pages works too).
2. Plugins → **Discover** → **Add i
ndex source**, then paste that https URL. Index sources accept `http:` / `https:` only, without cred

entials or a fragment.
3. Cards show the bilingual title and description — the index stores `descrip
tion` as an `{ "en": …, "zh": … }` object and **must contain `en`**; a Chinese-only value is rejecte
d by the validator. Installing uses the exact npm version.
Every version entry carries `engines.dsh` matching `package.json`; the Discover tab derives compatib
ility and the default version from it, and disables **Install** when no version is compatible. When
publishing a new version, append a `versions` entry with `version`, the real publish time as Unix se
conds in `publishTimestamp`, and `source.type: "npm"`.
## How the restart works
Three platform facts shape the design, all measured on a real machine:
1. A **detached** `powershell.exe` starts but never runs its `-EncodedCommand` script — silently, wi

th no error. The helper is spawned as a plain child instead.
2. Every process the Host starts inheri
ts Chromium's **job object** with kill-on-close, so anything the Host spawns dies with the applicati

on's main process. A helper that kills first and launches afterwards dies between those two steps.
3
. The **Task Scheduler** service resolves launches in its own process, outside that job, which is th
e only way to leave something running that outlives the kill.
So the order is inverted:

### HTTP routes
| Route | Purpose |

| `GET /desktop-restart/status` | `{ desktop, restarting, activeAgents, logPath }` |

## Known limitations
- **The restart is a hard kill** (`TerminateProcess`). The turn in flight is interrupted. Session hi

story and anything already written to disk are unaffected.
- **A restart is refused while a package
manager is installing into the profile** (`409 installing`). Three signals are checked: the plugin m
anager's own `plugin-manager/install-state` reports (`installing` / `cancelling` / `applying`) — aut
horitative, but it never reports completion, so a phase expires after ten minutes; a manifest writte
n within the last 10 seconds, which catches the moment an install *finishes*, since the lockfile is
written last; and, as a fallback, a live `node` process whose command line mentions `pnpm`. The 10-s
econd window is kept short on purpose: a finished install should not block a restart for longer than

it takes to notice. All three are best-effort and fail open.
- Only the Windows desktop app is supp
orted. On a plain `dsh web` Host the route answers `409 not-desktop` and the button falls back to re

loading the page.
- When the Scheduled Task channel is blocked by policy, the helper falls back to l
aunching PowerShell directly, which may flash a console window; the log marks it `(direct powershell

)`.
- No keyboard accelerator. The desktop shell hands shortcut combinations to a trusted native bri
dge before page handlers run, so a page-level listener cannot see them; adding one through the produ

ct's shortcut service would pull in a dependency this plugin does not otherwise need.
- `tasklist.ex
e` is *not* used for process detection: on a measured machine it answers `Access denied` (exit 1) in
this context, which would make every poll report the app as gone and start several copies. Detectio
n filters by image name first (`Get-Process -Name`) and then checks `.Path`.
